concerns.text: T024 specifies executing 'a sufficient number of episodes' but fails to enforce FR-003's mandatory requirement of exactly 1,000 episodes per (Tier, Threshold) combination. This semantic weakening risks under-powered statistical analysis and violates the explicit count constraint in the spec.

T023 describes iterating thresholds in 'uniform steps' but omits the specific FR-006 requirement to sweep from 0.0 to 1.0 in 0.1 increments. Without this explicit range and step size, the task allows a scope that does not satisfy the sensitivity analysis requirement.

T028 implements 'Linear/Quadratic' regression but omits the ANOVA implementation required by SC-004 to measure the statistical significance of the interaction term (p < 0.05). The task deliverable falls short of the success criteria it claims to support.

T030 relies on 'mean log-probability shift (from T021)' where T021 only promises 'logging' of shifts. There is no task to aggregate and calculate the mean shift metric required for the 'distillation cost-benefit ratio' defined in SC-002, creating a missing acceptance criterion.

T015 mandates 'mandatory caching logic' for generated graphs. This contradicts Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) and Principle III (Data Hygiene) which require graphs to be 'regenerated on-the-fly' or fetched from a canonical source to ensure fresh execution. Caching static artifacts risks violating the 'reproducible by re-running' constraint if the cache isn't strictly seed-based and versioned.

T029 implements 'inflection point detection logic' as a separate step. However, FR-006 and SC-001 define the inflection point as a result of the statistical regression (quadratic term significance), not a heuristic detector. This task risks implementing a solution that does not match the statistical method mandated by the spec.
